conventions.convention: Q is finite and acyclic; representations are finite-dimensional over F_q. The Euler form is χ(d,e)=Σ d_i e_i−Σ_(a:i→j) d_i e_j, and ⟨d,e⟩=χ(d,e)−χ(e,d).

Vertex charges lie in the open upper half-plane; phase is principal argument divided by π. Semistability requires every nonzero subobject to have phase at most the object's phase; stability requires strict inequality for proper nonzero subobjects.
The local Hall product is subobject first: (f⋆g)(L)=Σ_(U⊆L) f(U)g(L/U), the opposite of the generic quotient-first Hall product. Distinct embedded subobjects count separately.

Completion is the product over nonnegative dimension vectors, with formal degreewise convergence. With t=√q>0, the target twists are q^(−χ(e,d)) and t^(−⟨e,d⟩); skew integration includes t^χ(d,d)/|Aut(M)|.
The semistable-openness statement assumes AC for the declared projective scheme-construction and properness suppliers; the stack-point lemma explicitly inherits that assumption.
HN factors have strictly decreasing phases, and each phase factor includes all semistable objects, including strictly semistable objects.

load_bearing.statement: Over any field extension K/F_q, every finite-dimensional representation has a unique filtration with nonzero Z-semistable factors of strictly decreasing phases. For representations defined over F_q, the geometric filtration is Frobenius invariant and descends; geometric and finite-field semistability consequently agree.

For a finite acyclic quiver over F_q, the degree-completed subobject-first Hall product is associative and unital. The continuous maps I(f)=Σ f(M)/|Aut(M)| X^d(M) and J(f)=Σ t^χ(d(M),d(M)) f(M)/|Aut(M)| x^d(M) are unital algebra homomorphisms to the stated Euler and skew targets.

For any field K, finite-dimensional representations of a finite acyclic quiver form an abelian category with finite-dimensional Hom and Yoneda Ext¹, satisfying dim Hom(X,Y)−dim YExt¹(X,Y)=χ_Q(d(X),d(Y)). The displayed projective resolution has length one. Over F_q the category has a small finitary skeleton.

For any finite acyclic quiver over F_q and upper-half-plane vertex charges, A_all is the degreewise finite product of S_Z(φ) in decreasing phase order. Applying I or J gives equal completed ordered products for any two charge assignments; these products are units and give equal continuous conjugation automorphisms.
